SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints  
  • Severe headache for 4 days; started before fever  
  • Subjective fever (temperature not measured)  
  • Generalized myalgia; feels cold, no rigors reported  
  • Diffuse red, itchy rash; blanching on glass test  
- Associated negatives  
  • No photophobia (initial “yes” then “no” – conflict noted)  
  • No neck stiffness, no pain on neck movement  
  • No nausea/vomiting  
  • No cough, coryza, or ear pain  
  • No focal weakness; no paraesthesia  
- Travel history  
  • Returned from Thailand ≈1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell  
- Past medical history: denies chronic illnesses  
- Surgical history: none reported  
- Medications  
  • Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • No regular medications  
- Social history: not discussed beyond recent travel  
- Allergies: none known

Objective:
- No in-person physical examination performed (video consult)  
- Reported findings  
  • Rash: diffuse, red, itchy, blanching  
  • No documented vitals  
- Investigations: none performed; clinician recommends blood tests after in-person review

Assessment & Plan:

1. Febrile illness with headache post–Thailand travel  
   - Assessment: Suspected viral illness; must rule out mosquito-borne infections (e.g., dengue) and meningitis.  
   - Differential: Dengue fever; meningitis (bacterial or viral).  
   - Planned investigations: Urgent face-to-face examination; likely blood tests (full blood count, inflammatory markers, dengue screen as indicated).  
   - Treatment: Continue Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for symptom control.  
   - Referrals: Urgent same-day GP hub appointment; if unavailable, attend Emergency Department.

2. Generalized blanching pruritic rash  
   - Assessment: Likely viral exanthem associated with current febrile illness.  
   - Differential: Early meningococcal rash versus viral exanthem versus dengue-related rash.  
   - Planned investigations: As above (part of febrile work-up).  
   - Treatment: Symptomatic; reassess after examination.

Quality checks
• Missing/expected elements: objective vitals, full neurological exam, medication reconciliation (doses/frequency), immunization/travel prophylaxis history.  
• Internal conflicts: (1) Patient initially answered “Yep” to photophobia but immediately denied it—conflict noted. (2) Clinician addressed patient as “Ben” at end though patient identified as “John Doe.”  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor hesitations but clinical content understandable.
